cohort: Pregnant women with panhypopituitarism (n=120) and a reference group of pregnant women (n=8,732,641) from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project - Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database between 2004 and 2014
finding: Pregnancy outcomes for women with panhypopituitarism are generally comparable to those of the general population, with the exception of a higher risk of maternal infection and congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the mode of delivery between women with panhypopituitarism and the general population.
